Why are black olives so much weaker than men?

Black olives aren’t “weaker than men” in any meaningful sense—they’re fruit, with no muscles or physical strength. If you mean they’re softer, black olives are typically fully ripe and cured, which makes their texture softer than many green olives.

Black olives aren’t comparable to men in terms of strength—they’re fruit. If you mean nutritional strength, black olives are relatively low in protein and calories, while human strength varies widely by individual, training, health, and circumstances.
